new_statements.quote: El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva. A continuación se subrayan las sílabas donde hay acento.
new_statements.translation: The stress pattern in all varieties of the Kaqchikel language is fixed, its function is demarcative and its position is on the final syllable (oxytone or final stress). It is invariant under derivation. For that reason it need not be written, because it is predictable and has no distinctive function. Below, the syllables carrying stress are underlined.
new_statements.citation: Comunidad Linguistica Kaqchikel (ALMG); investigadores Juan Esteban Ajsivinac Sian, Lolmay Pedro Oscar Garcia Matzar, Martin Chacach Cutzal, Ixchel Elizabeth Alonzo Guajan. 2004. Gramatica descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel: Rutzijoxik rucholik ri Kaqchikel ch'ab'al. Chimaltenango: Comunidad Linguistica Kaqchikel, Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala.
new_statements.locator: Fonologia, section 'Acento', printed p.55 (PDF p.59; page image); exceptions printed pp.56-57 (-)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (printed p.55, FONOLOGIA, section 'Acento') and read it visually, since the djvu scanned layer is Cyrillic-garbled at this passage. The quoted sentence is there verbatim, accents included: 'El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva. A continuación se subrayan las sílabas donde hay acento.' Footnote 48 on the same page: 'Datos de la Variación Dialectal del Idioma Kaqchikel de la CLK, parte morfológica.' the PDF's metadata gives the tit…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the last syllable of the word (root, derived or compound), in every dialect; derivational suffixes therefore carry the stress (p.56 'Acento en el sufijo de derivacion (silaba final)'). OKMA 1997 p.20 adds that enclitics (directionals) attached to verbs and statives attract the stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in ALMG 2004 or OKMA 1997. Bennett 2018 (Glossa 3(1):67, fn.7, held): 'Secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel', and no phonotactic evidence for it.
new_statements.exceptions: ALMG 2004 p.56, citing the CLK Informe de Variacion Dialectal: (a) penultimate stress, 'no es muy comun en la mayoria de variantes', in a few native words (vakix 'vaca', tukur 'tecolote', tata 'senor', nana 'senora', b'alam 'tigre', anxa 'ajo', janila 'mucho') and in Spanish loans that are paroxytone (anma 'alma', paxa, alb'ertix 'arveja', xalma 'escalera'); in most variants vakix/tukur/nana/tata lose the second vowel (wakx, tukr, nan, tat) and then take regular final stress; (b) 'acento en silaba pesada' in very few words, only in the variants of Santa Maria de Jesus, Antigua Guatemala, Parramos, San Bartolome Milpas Altas and Magdalena Milpas Altas: in transitive verb forms the first vowel followed by glottal closure (usually before 3pl absolutive a'/e') takes the stress, e.g. xka'rutz'ot [ska?ruc'ot] 'el los mirara', xka'ruxim 'el los amarrara'; p.57: in Santa Maria de Jesus a syllable with diphthong ie (incl. loans) is heavy; in Alotenango the syllable with diphthong uo in some loans (pobre [puobra]). OKMA 1997 p.21: loans keep Spanish grave/esdrujula stress (kaxa, xara, anma); nana, tata first-syllable stress; Comalapa janila; Iximche' b'alam > b'ala with grave stress. Bennett 2016 sec.6.1: non-final stress in loans (anima) and some native words (janila).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('sílaba final de la palabra'); ALMG 2004 examples are citation forms with derived and compound words (nupatz'an, kumatz, xuk'am pe, ach-'ajmak, kowilaj kej); OKMA 1997 p.20 covers root, derived and compound words and says enclitics on verbs/statives attract stress (Xb'eruya' kan, tzalan pe). Nelson 2020 sec.3.1 gives instrumental confirmation on 1-4-syllable words from speakers of southern dialects, and quotes Brown, Maxwell & Little 2006:138 'in phrases, the primary stress falls on the last word'.
new_statements.identity_note: kaqc1272 is not a distinct language: Ethnologue 14/15 [ckd] 'South Central Cakchiquel/Kaqchikel' = 'Population 43,000 (1998 SIL). Region: Pan American highway west of Guatemala City' (San Lucas Sacatepequez, Santiago Sacatepequez, Sumpango, Milpas Altas towns, El Tejar, Zaragoza corridor), retired and merged into Kaqchikel [cak] = kaqc1270 in 2009. No ckd-specific description exists (SIL bibliography for the code = 3 literacy primers + a 2007 NT; Glottolog 0 descriptive refs). The stress statement quoted is the Kaqchikel language-level statement of the ALMG 2004 descriptive grammar, which asserts it 'en todas las variantes' and whose CLK dialect-survey data explicitly include the corridor towns (Sumpango, Santiago Sacatepequez, San Lucas Sacatepequez, Santa Lucia and San Bartolome Milpas Altas, El Tejar, Zaragoza). by our rule that each source is filed under the language's current Glottolog code (a retired code does not make a separate language) this should be filed under kaqc1270 (which already appears in webcat/ with a Berinstein 1979 ref), not as a separate entity; the same copies we hold serve kaqc1271/1274/1275/1277/1278/1279.

sources.note: p.55: stress fixed, demarcative, on the final syllable in all Kaqchikel variants, invariant under derivation, not. p.56: penultimate stress in a few native words and Spanish loans; heavy-syllable stress in a few transitive verb forms only in Santa Maria de Jesus, Antigua, Parramos, San Bartolome and Magdalena Milpas Altas; dialect data (CLK Informe de Variacion Dialectal) include the South Central corridor towns Sumpango, Santiago and San Lucas Sacatepequez, Santa Lucia / San Bartolome Milpas Altas, El Tejar, Zaragoza.

sources.note: p.20 'Acento': 'El Kaqchikel se caracteriza por tener acento fijo en una silaba determinada. El acento es agudo, lo que significa que la acentuacion siempre va a recaer en la silaba final de la palabra (radical, derivada o compuesta..). Al agregar encliticos a los verbos y estativos (como direccionales), el acento tiende a caer sobre estos.'; p.21: Spanish loans keep grave/esdrujula stress; exceptions nana, tata, Comalapa janila, Iximche' b'ala. Authors' varieties: Tecpan and San Andres Semetabaj.
